source_text: Puellis autem ferocissimam uaccam, ideoque praeter consuetudinem comparatam, diabolus praeparauit, sexui earum etiam de bestia aemulatus. Itaque dispoliatae et reticulis indutae producebantur. Horruit populus alteram respiciens puellam delicatam, alteram a partu recentem stillantibus mammis. Ita reuocatae et discinctis indutae. Prior Perpetua iactata est, et concidit in lumbos. Et ubi sedit, tunicam a latere discissam ad uelamentum femoris reduxit, pudoris potius memor quam doloris. Dehinc acu requisita et dispersos capillos infibulauit. Non enim decebat martyram sparsis capillis pati, ne in sua gloria plangere uideretur. Ita surrexit, et elisam Felicitatem cum uidisset, accessit et manum ei tradidit et suscitauit illam. Et ambae pariter steterunt. Et populi duritia deuicta reuocatae sunt in portam Sanauiuariam. Illic Perpetua a quodam tunc catechumino, Rustico nomine, qui ei adhaerebat, suscepta et quasi a somno expergita (adeo in spiritu et in extasi fuerat) circumspicere coepit, et instupentibus omnibus ait: Quando, inquit, proiciemur ad uaccam illam nescio quam? Et cum audisset quod iam euenerat, non prius credidit nisi quasdam notas uexationis in corpore et habitu suo recognouisset. Exinde accersitum fratrem suum, et illum catechuminum, adlocuta est dicens: In fide state et inuicem omnes diligite, et passionibus nostris ne scandalizemini.
thought_title: Perpetua covers herself and lifts Felicity
orientation: The redactor narrates Perpetua and Felicity as they are sent out to face the cow in the public games.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover for the girls the devil prepared a most ferocious cow, procured therefore contrary to custom, having envied their sex even in respect of the wild beast. Therefore stripped and dressed in nets they were led out. The people shuddered as they looked at one girl delicate, the other fresh from birth with breasts dripping. So they were recalled and dressed in loose robes. First Perpetua was tossed and she fell on her loins. And when she sat up, she drew back the tunic torn at the side toward a covering of the thigh, mindful of modesty rather than of pain. Then with a pin asked for she pinned up her scattered hair. For it was not proper for a martyr to suffer with scattered hair, lest she seem to lament in her glory. So she rose, and when she saw crushed Felicity, she went to her and gave her hand to her and raised her up. And both stood together. And with the hardness of the people overcome they were recalled into the Sanavivarian gate. There Perpetua, received by a certain at that time catechumen, by name Rusticus, who kept close to her, and awakened as if from sleep, for she had been so far in spirit and in trance, began to look around, and with all astounded she said: When, she said, are we to be thrown to that cow which I do not know. And when she heard that it had already happened, she did not believe until she recognized certain marks of mauling on her body and on her dress. Then with her brother summoned, and that catechumen, she spoke to them saying: Stand in faith and love one another all, and do not be made to stumble by our martyrdoms.

pass_b_english: For the young women the devil prepared a most ferocious cow, procured contrary to custom, because he envied their sex even in respect of the wild beast. They were led out stripped and dressed in nets. The crowd shuddered to look at one delicate girl and the other fresh from childbirth with dripping breasts. So they were called back and dressed in loose ungirded clothes.

Perpetua was tossed first and fell on her hips. As she sat, she drew her tunic, torn at the side, across to cover her thigh, mindful of modesty rather than pain. Then she asked for a pin and fastened up her scattered hair. For it was not fitting for a martyr to suffer with loose hair, lest she seem to be mourning in her glory. So she stood up, and when she saw Felicity crushed to the ground, she went to her and gave her a hand and raised her. And the two stood together. And when the hardness of the people was overcome, they were recalled to the Sanavivaria Gate.

There Perpetua was received by a man named Rusticus, then a catechumen, who stayed close to her, and as if woken from sleep — so deeply had she been in spirit and in ecstasy — she began to look around, and as everyone stared in amazement she said, “When are we to be thrown to that cow or whatever it is?” When she heard what had already happened, she did not believe it until she recognized certain marks of the attack on her body and clothing. Then she sent for her brother and that catechumen and spoke to them, saying, “Stand firm in faith and love one another, all of you, and do not be made to stumble by our martyrdoms.”
